newsitem.title: USA: Dakota Mining gets permits for Alaska project.
newsitem.headline: Dakota Mining gets permits for Alaska project.

text.p: USMX of Alaska, a wholly owned subsidiary of Denver-based Dakota Mining Corp, has received the state permits allowing production to start at the Illinois Creek Gold Mine in Interior Alaska, state officials said on Thursday.

"It's been a rigorous permitting process, but on that again shows that cooperation between state government, mining companies and local citizens can ensure environmentally sound development," Governor Tony Knowles said in a statement.

Opening the mine "sends a strong signal to the international mining community that profitable development can take place in rural Alaska. And second, it shows that a partnership between the state and the mining industry leads to high paying jobs for Alaskans," the Democratic governor said.

The mine, located about 300 miles west of Fairbanks and near the Yukon River village of Galena, is expected to produce about 55,000 ounces of gold and 390,000 ounces of silver a year during its estimated life of six to eight years, state officials said.
The Illinois Creek project was initially developed by Anchorage-based North Pacific Mining Corp, a subsidiary of a corporation owned by Alaska Natives.
Construction began last summer but was delayed by bad weather and other problems, state officials said. During the delay, the mine was purchased by Dakota Mining Corp.
Permits were issued to Dakota subsidiary, USMX of Alaska, officials said.

The Illinois Creek project will be the second major open-pit gold mine operating in Alaska. It will add to production from the Fort Knox Mine in Fairbanks, a project owned by Fairbanks Gold Mining Inc.
